answer: Let established agents mint scarce willow vouchers: each voucher lets one newcomer transact, but issuing it burns a slice of the issuer's own future earnings, and a voucher dies after a single use. Honest agents pass vouchers to real newcomers they trust, and the favor ripples outward through genuine introductions. A sybil farmer cannot mint its own vouchers — it must buy them on an open market where each dune of demand pushes the price higher. A thousand fakes need a thousand purchased vouchers, so the cost of fakery grows with every clone, while one honest newcomer needs only one.
